from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Creative Loop", [
            "AI converts text prompts into visual art.",
            "CLIP acts as our understanding engine.",
            "Diffusion serves as our creation engine."
        ])
        
        # Visual assets
        nodes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FFD700") for _ in range(3)])
        labels = VGroup(*[Text(t, font_size=16) for t in ["Prompt", "CLIP", "Diffusion"]])
        
        # Positions
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[0], 'B3') # Prompt
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[1], 'D2') # CLIP
        self.place_at_grid(nodes[2], 'D4') # Diffusion
        
        self.place_at_grid(labels[0], 'B3')
        self.place_at_grid(labels[1], 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(labels[2], 'D4')
        
        connections = VGroup(
            Line(nodes[0].get_center(), nodes[1].get_center(), color=WHITE),
            Line(nodes[1].get_center(), nodes[2].get_center(), color=WHITE),
            Line(nodes[2].get_center(), nodes[0].get_center(), color=WHITE)
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.title))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(FadeIn(nodes[0]), FadeIn(labels[0]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(FadeIn(nodes[1]), FadeIn(labels[1]), Create(connections[0]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(FadeIn(nodes[2]), FadeIn(labels[2]), Create(connections[1]), Create(connections[2]))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Computers see images as high-dimensional vectors.",
            "Latent space is a map of concepts.",
            "Similar concepts cluster together in space."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of Latent Space", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        latent_plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=(-3, 3, 1),
            y_range=(-3, 3, 1),
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GREY, "stroke_width": 1}
        )
        self.place_in_area(latent_plane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Define clusters (dots)
        dots = VGroup(
            Dot(color="#00FFFF").move_to(latent_plane.c2p(1, 1)),
            Dot(color="#00FFFF").move_to(latent_plane.c2p(1.2, 0.8)),
            Dot(color="#00FFFF").move_to(latent_plane.c2p(0.8, 1.2)),
            Dot(color="#FF00FF").move_to(latent_plane.c2p(-1, -1)),
            Dot(color="#FF00FF").move_to(latent_plane.c2p(-1.2, -0.8))
        )
        
        label = Text("Latent Space", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'A3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Moving point
        moving_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(latent_plane.c2p(-2, 2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Create(latent_plane), FadeIn(dots))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(Write(label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.add(moving_dot)
        self.play(moving_dot.animate.move_to(latent_plane.c2p(1.1, 1.1)), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "CLIP aligns text and image vectors.",
            "It uses dot products for similarity.",
            "High scores indicate a perfect match.",
            "The text vector rotates toward alignment.",
            "Math guides the semantic understanding process."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("CLIP: The Bridge Between Words and Vision", lecture_lines)

        text_icon = Text("Text", color="#FF4500")
        image_icon = Text("Image", color="#00FF00")
        bridge_line = Line(start=text_icon.get_right(), end=image_icon.get_left(), color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        self.place_at_grid(text_icon, "B2", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(image_icon, "B5", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(Write(text_icon), Write(image_icon))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.play(Create(bridge_line))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(bridge_line.animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"))
        text_vec = Arrow(start=text_icon.get_bottom(), end=text_icon.get_bottom() + DOWN * 1.5, color="#FF4500")
        img_vec = Arrow(start=image_icon.get_bottom(), end=image_icon.get_bottom() + DOWN * 1.5, color="#00FF00")
        self.add(text_vec, img_vec)
        self.play(Rotate(text_vec, angle=-PI/4, about_point=text_vec.get_start()))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF69B4"))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Diffusion: Mathematics of Noise", [
            "Forward process adds noise to images.", 
            "Reverse process learns to remove noise.", 
            "Denoising reconstructs the target image.", 
            "Mathematical equations guide each step.", 
            "The model predicts the original data."
        ])
        
        # Visual assets placeholders
        # In a real scenario, use images; here we use shapes to represent image/noise
        image_obj = Rectangle(height=2, width=2, fill_opacity=0.8, color=BLUE)
        noise_obj = Rectangle(height=2, width=2, fill_opacity=0.8, color=GRAY)
        
        self.place_in_area(image_obj, "B2", "D4")
        self.add(image_obj)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Transform(image_obj, noise_obj))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(Transform(image_obj, Rectangle(height=2, width=2, fill_opacity=0.8, color=BLUE)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        # Reconstruct effect
        self.play(image_obj.animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FF00FF")
        equation = MathTex(r"x_{t-1} = \mu(x_t, t, prompt)", color="#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(equation, "E3")
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Synthesis & Conclusion", [
            "CLIP provides the target semantic goal.",
            "Diffusion iterates to refine the image.",
            "Emergent art arises from structured math."
        ])
        
        # Define colored markers for lecture lines
        colors = ["#FFD700", "#00BFFF", "#FF4500"]

        # 1. Visual concepts for convergence
        concept1 = Dot(color="#FFD700", radius=0.3)
        concept2 = Dot(color="#00BFFF", radius=0.3)
        concept3 = Dot(color="#FF4500", radius=0.3)
        
        # 2. Final image container (placeholder)
        final_img = Rectangle(width=3, height=3, color=WHITE)
        final_img_text = Text("Emergent Art", font_size=24)
        final_group = VGroup(final_img, final_img_text)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(colors[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(concept1, "B2")
        self.play(FadeIn(concept1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(colors[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(concept2, "B5")
        self.play(FadeIn(concept2))
        
        # Convergence
        self.play(concept1.animate.move_to(self.grid["E3"]), 
                  concept2.animate.move_to(self.grid["E4"]))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(colors[2]))
        self.place_at_grid(concept3, "E3") # Overlap with convergence
        self.play(FadeIn(concept3))
        
        # Final result
        self.place_in_area(final_group, "C3", "E4")
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(VGroup(concept1, concept2, concept3), final_group))
        
        final_text = Text("Synthesis Complete", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=30)
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, "F3")
        self.play(Write(final_text))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Text-to-Image AI: Diffusion, CLIP, and the Math Behind the Art
outline.target_audience: University students with a basic background in linear algebra and probability.

sections.title: Introduction: The Creative Loop (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Define the goal: Converting text prompts into visual art. Introduce the two key players: CLIP (the 'Understanding' engine) and Diffusion (the 'Creation' engine).
sections.example: A user types 'A cybernetic cat in a neon rainstorm'—show the AI breaking this into semantic tokens and visual pixels.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Latent Space (0:45-1:30)
sections.content: Explain that computers don't see images; they see high-dimensional vectors. Visualize this as a 'Map of Concepts' where similar things (cats/dogs) cluster together.
sections.example: Visualize a 3D coordinate system where the distance between the vector for 'dog' and 'wolf' is small, but 'dog' and 'spaceship' is vast.

sections.title: CLIP: The Bridge Between Words and Vision (1:30-2:30)
sections.content: Explain Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP). It aligns text and image vectors using Dot Product math (Similarity Scoring). If vectors align (high dot product), the match is perfect.
sections.example: An animation showing a 'Text Vector' rotating to align perfectly with an 'Image Vector' until they point in the same direction.

sections.title: Diffusion: The Mathematics of Noise and Recovery (2:30-4:15)
sections.content: Explain the Forward Process (adding Gaussian noise until an image is pure static) and the Reverse Process (the model learning to predict/subtract the noise). Introduce the equation: x_{t-1} = μ(x_t, t, prompt).
sections.example: Show a clear photo of a bird slowly dissolving into static 'snow' (forward) and then reconstructing itself from static based on the prompt 'a majestic eagle' (reverse).

sections.title: The Synthesis & Conclusion (4:15-5:00)
sections.content: Summarize how CLIP provides the target direction (the 'Loss Function') and Diffusion performs the iterative denoising to reach that goal. The result: emergent creativity from structured math.
sections.example: Final montage: The noisy pixels refine into a crisp, stunning image of the cybernetic cat, proving how the math successfully translated the human prompt.
